newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 11.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 11.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:
A crisis in Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's cabinet eased on Monday when a senior communist minister turned away from an opposition-led campaign to sack a state governor.

Home (Interior) Minister Indrajit Gupta, who had earlier joined the opposition in criticising Romesh Bhandari, governor of India's most populous Uttar Pradesh state, told the upper house of parliament he had no plans to sack the official.
The Lok Sabha, the lower house of parliament, was due to debate the issue later this week.

India's unstable political environment, directionless economic policies, and a deterioration in its macroeconomic balances have led Moody's Investors Service Inc to take an unfavorable outlook on the nation's Baa3 sovereign rating, the agency said.
Moody's, which upgraded India's rating from Ba2 to Baa3 in December, 1994, recently assessed potential pressure on the rating over an 18- to 24-month horizon.
The Indian rupee opened Tuesday at 35.855/860 per dollar, little changed from Monday's close of 35.85/86, dealers said. It is seen trading between 35.85 and 35.87 per dollar on Tuessday, they said.
Indian shares ended lower on Monday as speculators -- who were bidders after last month's pro-business budget -- unwound long positions, traders said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange tumbled 107.30 points, or 2.8 percent, to close at 3768.74.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index lost 48.55 points, or 4.3 percent, to 1,078.70.
The Delhi share index was down 34.17 points, or 4.13 percent, to 794.16.
Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd's two billion rupee ($55.8 million) debt issue has been four times oversubscribed, the Financial Express daily reported on Tuesday.
Foreign investors are wary of paying a premium to the domestic price for Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd's planned Global Depositary Receipt issue, the Asian Age daily reported on Tuesday.
